questions.q: What did Joab do when he knew the king’s heart was against Absalom?
questions.a: Joab sent to Tekoa and brought a wise woman from there to act as if she had been in mourning for a long time.

questions.q: What did Joab want the wise woman to do?
questions.a: Joab wanted the wise woman to pretend to be a mourner and to go speak to the king the words Joab told her to say.

questions.q: When the wise woman went to the king, whom did she say she was?
questions.a: The wise woman told the king she was a widow.

questions.q: What did the wise woman tell the king her two sons had done?
questions.a: She told the king that her two sons fought in a field, and one struck the other and killed him.

questions.q: What did the wise woman tell the king she was afraid would happen to her remaining son?
questions.a: She said she was afraid the whole clan would kill her remaining son, destroying her heir and leaving no descendants to preserve her family’s name.

questions.q: Why did the wise woman ask the king to remember Yahweh his God?
questions.a: She asked the king to remember Yahweh so that the avenger of blood would not destroy her son.

questions.q: Who did the king swear by when he told the woman that not one hair of her son would fall to the ground?
questions.a: The king swore by the life of Yahweh.

questions.q: Why did the woman say the king had been doing the wrong thing?
questions.a: The woman said the king was acting badly because he had not brought back his own banished son.

questions.q: What did the woman say God does instead of taking away life?
questions.a: She said that God forgives people who have sinned against him so that they can once more be in a good relationship with him.

questions.q: Why did the woman say she came to speak to the king?
questions.a: She said she came because the people had frightened her, and she hoped the king would listen and deliver her.

questions.q: What did the woman say about the king?
questions.a: She said that what the king says will comfort her, because he is like an angel of God, and he knows how to determine what is right and what is wrong.

questions.q: What did the king ask the woman?
questions.a: The king asked the woman if Joab arranged for her to do all this.

questions.q: Why did Joab have the woman go to the king?
questions.a: Joab did that to try to get David to feel differently about this matter.

questions.q: What did Joab do when the king told him to bring Absalom back?
questions.a: Joab lay facedown on the ground in honor and gratitude to the king.

questions.q: What instructions did the king give about Absalom?
questions.a: The king said that Absalom could return to his own house but could go and speak with the king.

questions.q: What was notable about Absalom’s appearance?
questions.a: He was so handsome that people throughout Israel praised Absalom for being a very handsome man. He did not seem to have any flaws in any part of his body. His hair was long, thick, and heavy.

questions.q: How long did Absalom live in Jerusalem without seeing the king’s face?
questions.a: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years, during which David still did not allow Absalom to come and speak with him.

questions.q: What did Absalom tell his servants to do after Joab refused to come to him?
questions.a: Absalom told his servants to go and burn Joab’s barley field with fire.

questions.q: What did Absalom want Joab to do?
questions.a: Absalom wanted Joab to go to the king and ask why he had come from Geshur, and to say that he wanted to come and speak with him.

questions.q: What did the king do when Absalom bowed before him?
questions.a: The king kissed Absalom on the cheek to show that he was no longer hostile to him.

commentary.text: He is admitted to his father's presence.

Verses 1–20 We may notice here, how this widow pleads God's mercy, and his clemency toward poor guilty sinners. The state of sinners is a state of banishment from God. God pardons none to the dishonour of his law and justice, nor any who are impenitent; nor to the encouragement of crimes, or the hurt of others.

David was inclined to favour Absalom, yet, for the honour of his justice, he could not do it but upon application made for him, which may show the methods of Divine grace. It is true that God has thoughts of compassion toward poor sinners, not willing that any should perish; yet he is only reconciled to them through a Mediator, who pleads on their behalf. God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, and Christ came to this land of our banishment, to bring us to God.

Nothing is said of Absalom's wisdom and piety. All here said of him is, that he was very handsome. A poor commendation for a man that had nothing else in him valuable. Many a polluted, deformed soul dwells in a fair and comely body. And we read that he had a very fine head of hair. It was a burden to him, but he would not cut it as long as he could bear the weight. That which feeds and gratifies pride, is not complained of, though uneasy. May the Lord grant us the beauty of holiness, and the adorning of a meek and quiet spirit! Only those who fear God are truly happy.

By his insolent carriage toward Joab, Absalom brought Joab to plead for him. By his insolent message to the king, he gained his wishes. When parents and rulers countenance such characters, they will soon suffer the most fatal effects. But did the compassion of a father prevail to reconcile him to an impenitent son, and shall penitent sinners question the compassion of Him who is the Father of mercies?
